title: Site Health
description: Runs WordPress's `/wp-site-health/v1/tests/{id}` async checks and reports results.

documentation.purpose: Runs WordPress's async site-health checks (`/wp-site-health/v1/tests/{id}`) in parallel on mount and on user re-run. Surfaces a per-test card with status (Good / Recommended / Critical) and a HTML description; the toolbar summarizes counts per category and offers a re-run button. Five tests today: WordPress.org communication, background updates, loopback requests, HTTPS status, authorization header.

reads.purpose: One request per test id; runs `Promise.all` over all five. Each returns `{ status, label, description }`.

states.renders: Toolbar Re-run button shows loading; cards without results show Spinner.
Cards already-completed show their status pill; remaining cards show Spinner.
All cards show status + description; toolbar shows category counts.
Error text below the toolbar (plus per-test error captured in results).
That test's card shows status=critical with `err.message` as description.

interactions.effect: Reset results + run all tests in parallel.

a11y.focus-management: Native focus order — toolbar button + card content.
a11y.screen-reader: Per-test status surfaces as a Badge with intent (`success` / `warning` / `error` / `neutral`). The badge text is the live status; no aria-live region announces completion.

constraints.note: Test descriptions arrive as HTML from `/wp-site-health/v1/tests/{id}`. WordPress core authors these strings; we render via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. ESLint disable comment in source notes the trust boundary.
Each test's request is wrapped in try/catch so one failing test doesn't reject the `Promise.all`. Failed tests show as critical with the error message — preserves partial results.
Tests are hard-coded module-scope. WordPress site-health is plugin-extensible (`site_status_tests` filter); the shell doesn't yet honor this.

design-system-leakage.purpose: Status pills + cards + heading + re-run button.
